newsitem.title: BELGIUM: ASLK/CGER to repay Confederation Life bond holders.
newsitem.headline: ASLK/CGER to repay Confederation Life bond holders.

text.p: Belgian bank ASLK/CGER, a unit of Belgian-Dutch insurance and banking group Fortis, will repay all investors to whom it sold bonds of Canadian insurer Confederation Life Insurance Co, the bank said in a statement on Thursday.
On March 26 a Belgian court ordered the bank to repay 135 customers who had sued the bank for damages relating to the defaulted subordinated bonds.
A bank spokesman told Reuters that the cost to the bank would be just over 400 million Belgian francs.
"Although the judgment does not oblige the bank to do so, it has decided to repay all investors who subscribed to these Eurobonds via us," the statement said.
The 135 investors had sued the bank, arguing that the bank's sales agents should have made it clearer that the bonds were subordinated. The Canadian insurer defaulted on the paper in 1994.

The court case was closely followed by the Belgian financial community because it raised the question to what extent banks selling Eurobonds to customers could be held responsible for the issuer's default.

At the time of the judgment a bank official told Reuters that when Confederation defaulted investors owning regular bonds had also lost their money and that the subordinated bonds sold by ASLK did have a subordination clause on the security itself.
ASLK/CGER, which is 49.9 percent owned by Fortis, earned 1996 group net profit of 6.82 billion francs.
-- Geert De Clercq, Brussels Newsroom +32 2 287 6813, Fax +32 2 230 7710
